newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty lunges upward on currency position trimming.
newsitem.headline: Zloty lunges upward on currency position trimming.

text.p: The zloty strengthened against the basket of currencies as banks shortened foreign currency positions to take advantage of high one-day deposit rates on the cash-short Polish money market, dealers said.

Dealers said client-drive trade was light on Wednesday and bank position adjustments took centre stage, driving the zloty to close at 1.96/1.89 pct from the trading band centre, firmer than Tuesday's close at 1.84/1.80 percent.
"The difference between zloty deposits and foreign currency depos is too large to keep long currency positions," said one foreign bank dealer in Warsaw.
The zloty was at 2.7825/40 per dollar, flat from Tuesday's 2.7830/40 and at 1.8381/98 per mark, up from 1.8410/15.
On the money market, overnight rates closed at 24.4/24.7 percent, up from Tuesday's 23.4/24.4 and tomorrow/next rates were at 24.5/24.7 percent from yesterday's 23.2/24.6.
Dealers said the money market would likely remain strapped for cash until late next week as monthly tax payments around September 20 would likely keep rates from dropping earlier.
In August reserve money, a cornerstone of the central bank's monetary policy this year, grew to 32.510 billion zlotys, within the target band of 31.93-32.63 billion.
At tomorrow's 800 million zloty tender of fixed 16-percent two-year and 12-percent five-year bonds yields are expected to hold flat from the last auction on August 22.

Foreign investors, who have been absent from recent treasury tenders, are likely to return on Thursday and bid mainly for the attractive two-year bond, which yielded around 19.9 percent at the last auction on August 22, dealers said.
The Central Statistical Office said on Wednesday that food prices rose 1.4 percent in the September 1-10 period after falling 0.1 percent in the previous 10 days.
